applications.description: Erection of self-storage warehouse (use class B8) with associated parking and circulation area

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Compliance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above.

conditions.summary: Statement of construction practice
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until a statement of construction practice has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Statement of construction practice shall include full details of: a) The construction vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles and associated traffic management measures. b) Methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway from the development hereby approved. c) Measures to control the emissions of dust and dirt during construction. d) How the statement of construction practice will be made publicly available by the developer.

conditions.summary: Vehicle access areas surfaced and drained
conditions.text: Development shall not be brought into use until all areas shown on the approved plans to be used by vehicles, including roads, footpaths, cycle tracks, loading and servicing areas and vehicle parking space have been fully laid out, surfaced and drained such that loose materials and surface water does not discharge or transfer onto the highway.

conditions.summary: Visibility splays (2.4m x 43m)
conditions.text: The access hereby approved shall not be brought into use until works have been undertaken to provide the visibility splays of 2.4m x 43m shown on Drwg. No. 23-194-T-100 Rev D (General Arrangement) to an adoptable standard. These visibility splays shall be retained clear of all obstruction to visibility greater than 600mm in height above the adjoining carriageway for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Disabled parking bays provision
conditions.text: Development shall not be brought into use until the approved disabled parking bays have been laid out and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Cycle and motorcycle parking provision
conditions.text: Development shall not be brought into use until the approved cycle/motorcycle parking and facilities have been provided. The approved facilities shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Car Park and Servicing Management Plan
conditions.text: Development shall not be brought into use until a Car Park and Servicing Management Plan (including timescales) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall be fully implemented, and the development thereafter operated in accordance with the approved timescales.

conditions.summary: Electric Vehicle Charging Points
conditions.text: Development shall not be brought into use until full details and a scheme for provision of Electric Vehicle Charging Points, cable enabled spaces and associated infrastructure have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The facilities shall be provided prior to the development being brought into use and retained and maintained thereafter as approved for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Off-site highway works (access and restrictions)
conditions.text: Development shall not be brought into use until the off-site highway works as shown in principle on Drwg. No. 23-194-T-100 Rev D (General Arrangement) comprising site access alterations (incl. widening, dropped kerbs and tactile paving) and extending 'no waiting' and 'no loading' on-street restriction markings at Atkinson Street have been fully delivered.

conditions.summary: External walling materials details and samples
conditions.text: Construction of external walls to any building subject of this permission shall not take place until details and samples of all external walling materials have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The walls shall be constructed from the approved materials.

conditions.summary: Boundary walls, fences and screening details
conditions.text: No part of the development shall be brought into use until details of the position, design, materials and type of all walls and/or fences or permanent boundary/screening treatment, whether or not shown to be erected on the approved plans, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Such walls and fences must also be erected in accordance with the approved details, before the land/buildings to which they relate are occupied, and shall thereafter be retained for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Construction Environmental Management Plan (Biodiversity)
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of development, a Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP:Biodiversity) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The CEMP (Biodiversity) shall put in place measures to retain and protect the 0.48 Habitat Units (A-1 On-site Habitat Baseline) and enhanced by 0.11 Habitat Units to 0.59 Habitat Units (A-3 On-site Area Habitat Enhancement) as identified in the Biodiversity Net Gain Calculation prepared by James Blake Associates (Ref: JBA 24/415 ECO2a SW/NP Rev A, dated 8th October 2024) and include measures to avoid or reduce impacts during demolition and construction, location and timings of sensitive works to avoid harm to biodiversity features, and the role of a responsible person (Ecological Clerk of Works).

conditions.summary: Hard and soft landscape works details
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall not be brought into use until full details of both hard and soft landscape works, including a dated implementation programme (inclusive of any phasing), have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Hard landscape works shall include proposed finished levels, car parking layouts, access areas, hard surfacing, structures, and existing trees with RPAs. Soft landscape works shall include planting plans, specifications and schedule of plants.

conditions.summary: Landscape works implementation and verification
conditions.text: All hard and soft landscaping works shall be carried out in accordance with the implementation programme approved pursuant to condition 14 above. On completion of those works a Verification Report(s) that clearly demonstrates that the approved landscaping works have been fully implemented as approved shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved implementation programme. The development shall not be brought into use until such time as the submitted verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Landscape management plan
conditions.text: A landscape management plan, including long term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the occupation of the development. The landscape management plan shall be for the lifetime of the development and shall be carried out as approved.

conditions.summary: Nesting birds protection (March to August restriction)
conditions.text: No works to or removal of hedgerows, trees or shrubs with bird-nesting potential shall take place between 1st March and 31st August inclusive, unless a competent ecologist has undertaken a careful, detailed check of vegetation or built structures for active birds' nests immediately before (within 24 hours) the works commence and provided written confirmation that no birds will be harmed and/or that there are appropriate measures in place to protect nesting bird interest on site.

conditions.summary: Bat mitigation licence requirement (demolition)
conditions.text: No works shall commence to demolish the existing office building unless the Local Planning Authority has been provided with either: a) The Mitigation Method Statement and licence issued by Natural England pursuant to Regulation 53 of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2010 authorising the specified activity to go ahead; or b) (Where a Low Impact Class Licence is used) a copy of the Site Registration Form, Licence Return and the confirmation e-mail from Natural England that the site has been registered, together with a statement from the appointed ecologist of the proposed mitigation and compensation roosting features; or c) a statement in writing from an appropriately qualified ecologist to the effect that it does not consider that the specified activity will require a licence.

conditions.summary: Integral bat roosting features in approved building
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of building works, a Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority of: integral bat roosting features within the approved building. Features that are not integral will only be considered for approval if an appropriately qualified ecologist provides assurance that, following discussions with the building architect, integral features are not possible. The agreed Plan shall show the number, specification of the bat roosting features and where they will be located, together with a timetable for implementation and commitment to being installed under the instruction of an appropriately qualified bat consultant. All approved features shall be installed prior to the building on which they are located being brought into use and retained in the manner as approved thereafter.

conditions.summary: Interim and temporary drainage measures during construction
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until details and a method statement for the interim and temporary drainage measures to be adopted during the site clearance and construction phases that address the key flood and drainage risks and any other flood and drainage risks subsequently identified, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This information shall provide full details of who will be responsible for maintaining such temporary systems and demonstrate how the site will be drained to ensure there is no increase in the off-site flows, nor any pollution, debris and sediment to any third-party land or public highway or any receiving watercourse or sewer system.

conditions.summary: Flood Risk Assessment and SuDS Strategy compliance
conditions.text: The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details contained within the Flood Risk Assessment and SuDS Strategy prepared by WE (Ref: 23104-FRA-RP-01 Rev C01, dated 29 October 2024) and shown in the accompanying Drwg. No. 23104-SWD-DP-01 Rev C01 (Sustainable Drainage Strategy), unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Phase II Site Investigation and Remediation Strategy
conditions.text: The approved Phase I Desk Study report indicates that a Phase II Site Investigation is necessary, and therefore development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Phase II Site Investigation Report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where remediation measures are shown to be necessary in the Phase II Report and/or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Remediation Strategy demonstrating how the site will be made suitable for the intended use has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination notification procedure
conditions.text: If remediation is unable to proceed in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy, or where significant unexpected contamination is encountered, or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, the Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately and operations on the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. An amended or new Remediation Strategy and/or Soil Importation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any further remediation works which shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the revised approved Strategy.

conditions.summary: Remediation works implementation and verification
conditions.text: Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: No external storage of plant, materials or products
conditions.text: No external storage of plant, materials and/or products shall take place on any part of the site.

conditions.summary: Self-storage use restriction (Class B8)
conditions.text: The hereby approved building shall not be used other than for self-storage purposes nor for any other purpose in Class B8 use of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 or in any statutory instrument revoking or re-enacting that Order with or without modification.

conditions.summary: Training and Employment Plan
conditions.text: No development shall take place until a Training and Employment Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall set out how the developer will co-operate with Employment Leeds in order to promote training and employment opportunities for local people from the start of the tendering process for the construction of the development, throughout the period when the hereby approved development is under construction. The measures identified shall be implemented in accordance with the approved plan.

conditions.summary: Development to commence within three years of permission
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission. Imposed pursuant to the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above. For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

conditions.summary: External walling and roofing materials approval and samples
conditions.text: Construction of external walls or superstructure to any building above slab level subject of this permission shall not take place until details and samples of all external walling and roofing materials have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Samples shall be made available on site prior to the commencement of building works, for inspection by the Local Planning Authority which shall be notified in writing of their availability. The building works shall be constructed from the materials thereby approved and retained thereafter.

conditions.summary: Coal mining intrusive investigations and remediation
conditions.text: No above ground development shall commence until: a) a scheme of intrusive investigations has been carried out on site to establish the risks posed to the development by past shallow coal mining activity; and b) any remediation works and/or mitigation measures to address land instability arising from coal mining legacy, as may be necessary, have been implemented on site: and c) a signed statement or declaration prepared by a suitably competent person confirming that the site is, or has been made, safe and stable for the approved development. has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Remediation Strategy for contaminated land
conditions.text: Development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Remediation Strategy demonstrating how the site will be made suitable for the intended use has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all works and for the provision of Verification Reports.

conditions.summary: Contingency for unexpected contamination or soil importation
conditions.text: If remediation is unable to proceed in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy, or where significant unexpected contamination is encountered, or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, the Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately and operations on the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. An amended or new Remediation Strategy and/or Soil Importation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any further remediation works which shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the revised approved Strategy.

conditions.summary: Remediation works implementation and verification
conditions.text: Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Cycle parking and facilities provision
conditions.text: Notwithstanding the approved details, works above the ground floor slab level shall not commence until full details of cycle parking and facilities have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved cycle parking and facilities shall be provided prior to first occupation of the development and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Vehicle parking, roads and servicing areas to be fully laid out and drained
conditions.text: Development shall not be occupied until all areas shown on the approved plans to be used by vehicles, including roads, footpaths, cycletracks, loading and servicing areas and vehicle parking space have been fully laid out, surfaced and drained such that loose materials and surface water does not discharge or transfer onto the highway. These areas shall not be used for any other purpose thereafter.

conditions.summary: Statement of Construction Practice including routing, dust and mud control
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until a statement of construction practice has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Statement of Construction Practice shall include full details of: a) The construction vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles and associated traffic management measures. b) Methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway from the development hereby approved. c) Measures to control the emissions of dust and dirt during construction. d) How the statement of construction practice will be made publicly available by the developer.

conditions.summary: Electric Vehicle Charging Points and cable-enabled spaces
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until full details and a scheme for provision of Electric Vehicle Charging Points, cable enabled spaces and associated infrastructure have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The facilities shall be provided prior to first occupation of the development, retained and maintained thereafter as approved for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Bin stores and waste storage provisions
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details for the provision of bin stores (including siting, materials and means of enclosure) and (where applicable) storage of wastes and access for their collection shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved measures shall be implemented in full before the use commences and shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Service yard and turning area to remain free from obstruction
conditions.text: The service yard and turning area as shown on approved plan ref (561)2413-GWP-01-00-D-A-(PA)-0002 P04 shall remain free from any obstruction including the entirety of the area required for access and turning of large articulated lorries. This shall remain in place and managed as such for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Accessible lift installation for first-floor office use
conditions.text: The first-floor of the office shall not be occupied or brought into use as an office, storage or any other purposes ancillary to the B2/B8 main use of the building until the approved accessible lift set out in drawing ref: '(561)2413-GWP-01-ZZ-D-A-(PA)-0008 rev: P05' is installed and brought into use. The accessible lift facilities shall be implemented, retained and maintained thereafter as approved for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Renewable energy sources and BREEAM Excellent certification
conditions.text: Development shall not be occupied until full details and specification relating to renewable energy sources and technologies, as indicated in submitted supplementary information ref: Policy EN4 statement (05.04.2025) and BREEAM pre-assessment summary report (29.05.2025), has been assessed and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development is required to secure a BREEAM excellent certificate in order to comply with policy EN2.

conditions.summary: Hard and soft landscaping works and implementation programme
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until full details of both hard and soft landscape works, including an implementation programme, have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Hard landscape layout plans and annotated cross sections including dimensions, colours, materials, construction etc. detailing: (a) boundary treatments, (b) types of hard surfacing, (c) minor artefacts and structures (e.g. refuse or other storage units, signs, lighting etc.), Soft landscape details including: (d) planting plans for trees, hedges, meadow areas etc (e) written specifications (including soil depths, cultivation and other operations associated with establishment) and, (f) schedules of trees noting species, planting sizes and proposed numbers/densities.

conditions.summary: Tree replacement within five years if removed, uprooted or dies
conditions.text: If within a period of five years from the date of the planting of any tree is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies, or becomes, in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority, seriously damaged or defective, another tree of the same species and size as that originally planted shall be planted in the same location as soon as reasonably possible and no later than the first available planting season, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Development to commence within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Compliance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above.

conditions.summary: External surfacing materials approval
conditions.text: Construction of hardsurfaced areas shall not take place until details and samples of all external surfacing materials have been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Retention and protection of approved trees
conditions.text: Within 5 years of first use of the development hereby approved, no approved retained trees shall be cut down, uprooted or destroyed, nor shall any tree be pruned, topped or lopped or suffer root severance (other than in accordance with the approved plans and particulars). In the event of any such works being carried out without having first sought and received written approval from the LPA the following actions shall be undertaken: (a) Within one month of the removal, uprooting, damage or loss of any retained tree, a replacement planting scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA. That replacement planting scheme shall include the replacement of trees in accordance with current policies (e.g. LAND 2 'Development and Trees') by semi-mature size trees (circumference 25/30cm) or an equivalent offsite mitigation planting scheme, where on site provision is not possible. The mitigation planting scheme shall be implemented in the first planting season following the receipt of the written approval of those details by the LPA. (b) Within one month of a pruning, topping, lopping or root severance of a retained tree, a Professional Arboricultural Report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the LPA. The report shall include a full assessment of the unauthorised work, remediation proposals and implementation programme. Within one week following the implementation of the planting scheme agreed pursuant to a) or b) above, documentation shall be submitted to the LPA that evidences the works have been carried out in accordance with the agreed details.

conditions.summary: Tree and habitat protection during works
conditions.text: No works shall commence (including any demolition, site clearance, groundworks or drainage etc.) until all existing trees, hedges and vegetation shown to be retained on the approved plans are fully safeguarded by protective fencing and ground protection in accordance with the approved Tree and Habitat Protection Plan (Dwg. No. RHS004_LTHT_P_104) received on the 6th December 2024 and the specifications and the provisions of British Standard 5837 (2012) Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction. Exclusion zones shall be clearly signposted to ensure access is prohibited and shall be retained for the entirety of the construction phase. NOTE Only the BS5837 default barrier with the scaffold framework shall be employed. Such measures shall be retained for the full duration of any demolition and/or approved works. Exclusion zones shall be enforced to ensure no equipment, machinery or materials shall be used, stored or burnt within any protected area nor shall any ground levels within these zones be altered, nor any excavations undertaken including the provision of any underground services.

conditions.summary: Landscape management plan
conditions.text: A landscape management plan, including long term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to first use of the development hereby approved. The Management Plan must conform to Leeds City Council's Landscape Management Plans and associated checklist. The management plan shall thereafter be implemented within the first available planting season and carried out in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Statement of construction practice
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until a statement of construction practice has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the statement of construction practice shall include full details of: a) the construction vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles and associated traffic management measures. b) methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway from the development hereby approved. The approved details shall be implemented at the commencement of works on site and shall thereafter be retained and employed until completion of the works on site.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination discovery protocol
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately where unexpected significant contamination is encountered during any development works and operations in the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. Where remediation of unexpected significant contamination is considered by the Local Planning Authority to be necessary, a Remediation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the recommencement of development on the affected part of the site. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all remediation works and for the provision of verification information. Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all necessary verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Testing and approval of imported soils
conditions.text: Any soil or soil forming materials brought to site for use in garden areas, soft landscaping, public open space or for filling and level raising shall be tested for contamination and suitability for use. A methodology for testing these soils shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to these materials being imported onto site. The methodology shall include information on the source of the materials, sampling frequency, testing schedules and criteria against which the analytical results will be assessed (as determined by risk assessment). Testing shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved methodology. Relevant evidence, assessment and verification information shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to the site or phase of the site being brought into use.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Gain Plan approval requirement
conditions.text: Development may not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority; and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan. The planning authority, for the purposes of determining whether to approve a Biodiversity Gain Plan, if one is required in respect of this permission would be Leeds City Council.

conditions.summary: Accordance with approved plans

conditions.summary: External walling and roofing materials to match existing

The intrusive site investigations and remedial works shall be carried out in accordance with authoritative UK guidance.

conditions.summary: Signed statement confirming site safety and stability post-remediation
conditions.text: Prior to the occupation of the development, or it being taken into beneficial use, a signed statement or declaration prepared by a suitably competent person confirming that the site is, or has been made, safe and stable for the approved development shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This document shall confirm the methods and findings of the intrusive site investigations and the completion of any remedial works and/or mitigation necessary to address the risks posed by past coal mining activity.

conditions.summary: Notification and remediation of unexpected contamination
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately where unexpected significant contamination is encountered during any development works and operations in the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. Where remediation of unexpected significant contamination is considered by the Local Planning Authority to be necessary, a Remediation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the recommencement of development on the affected part of the site. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all remediation works and for the provision of verification information. Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all necessary verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. In the event that no unexpected significant contamination is encountered, written confirmation shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority prior to occupation of the site.

conditions.summary: Warehouse operational hours (08:00-18:00 Mon-Fri, 08:00-12:00 Sat)
conditions.text: The warehouse building shall only be used between the hours of 08:00 - 18:00 hours Mondays to Fridays and 08:00 hours and 12:00 (midday) hours on Saturdays.

conditions.summary: Use restriction to Class B8 (warehouse) only, no retail sales

conditions.summary: Walls, roof and structures from approved materials

conditions.summary: Cycle and motorcycle parking provision

conditions.summary: Vehicle areas to be fully laid out, surfaced and drained

These areas shall not be used for any other purpose thereafter.

conditions.summary: Construction Practice Statement implementation
conditions.text: The approved details in the supplied Statement of Construction Practice shall be implemented at the commencement of works on site and shall thereafter be retained and employed until completion of the works on site. The Statement on Construction practice shall be made publicly available for the lifetime of the construction phase of the development in accordance with the approved method of publicity.

conditions.summary: Noisy construction activity hours limit
conditions.text: Times of noisy construction activity shall be limited to 0800-1800 Monday to Friday; 0900-1300 Saturday, with no working on Sundays or Bank Holiday.

conditions.summary: External lighting scheme approval required
conditions.text: No external lighting shall be installed unless a scheme has previously been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall be installed and retained thereafter in accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Music or amplified sound not audible at site boundary
conditions.text: Any music or amplified sound including tannoy systems used shall not be audible from any point on the site boundary.

conditions.summary: Electric Vehicle Charging Points and infrastructure provision
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until full details and a scheme for provision of Electric Vehicle Charging Points, cable enabled spaces and associated infrastructure have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The facilities shall be provided prior to first occupation of the development, retained and maintained thereafter as approved for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination notification and remediation
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately where unexpected significant contamination is encountered during any development works and operations in the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. Where remediation of unexpected significant contamination is considered by the Local Planning Authority to be necessary, a Remediation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the recommencement of development on the affected part of the site. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all remediation works and for the provision of verification information. Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all necessary verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. In the event that no unexpected significant contamination is encountered, written confirmation shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority prior to occupation of the site.

conditions.summary: Tree protection and arboricultural monitoring
conditions.text: a) No works shall commence (including any demolition, site clearance, ground works or drainage etc.) until all existing trees shown to be retained on the approved plans are fully safeguarded by protective fencing and ground protection in accordance with approved plans and the specifications and the provisions of British Standard 5837 (2012) Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. b) Evidence shall be submitted, such as a written appointment (including site specifics), that confirms that a qualified Arboriculturist/competent person has been appointed to carry out this Arboricultural monitoring/supervision. c) Seven days written notice shall be given to the Local Planning Authority that the protection measures are in place prior to demolition/ approved works commencing, to allow inspection and approval of the protection measures as implemented on site. d) No equipment, machinery or materials shall be used, stored or burnt within any protected area. Ground levels within these areas shall not be altered, nor any excavations undertaken including the provision of any underground services/drainage, without the prior written approval of the Local Planning Authority.

applications.address: Rocol Ltd Rocol House Wakefield Road Swillington Leeds LS26 8BS

Imposed pursuant to the provisions of Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

conditions.summary: Development to accord with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above. For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

conditions.summary: Approval of replacement windows, cladding and condenser cage details
conditions.text: No works shall take place in respect of the approved development until full details of the proposed replacement windows, cladding and condenser cage have been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The proposed alterations and condenser cage shall thereafter be constructed in accordance with the approved details. In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Landscape management plan to be submitted and approved
conditions.text: A landscape management plan, including long term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the occupation of the development. The Management Plan must conform to Leeds City Council's Landscape Management Plans (Landscape Guidance No.2) and associated checklist. The landscape management plan shall be for the lifetime of the development and shall be carried out as approved. To ensure successful aftercare of landscaping.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity Gain Plan approval required before development commencement
conditions.text: The effect of paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 is that planning permission granted for development of land in England is deemed to have been granted subject to the condition (biodiversity gain condition) that development may not begin unless: (a) a Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the planning authority; and (b) the planning authority has approved the plan.

conditions.summary: Building materials as shown on elevations plan

conditions.summary: Compliance with revised drainage and site plans

PROPOSED BUILDING PLANS. 03 MARCH 2025, maintaining a 2.1m easement at all levels submitted, and the drainage strategy accepted in the original application 22/02393/FU. conditions.summary: Cycle and motorcycle parking facilities

The approved cycle/motorcycle parking and facilities shall be provided prior to first occupation of the development and retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development. In the interests of highway safety and promoting sustainable travel opportunities.

conditions.summary: Vehicle areas surfacing and drainage
conditions.text: Development shall not be occupied until all areas shown on the approved plans to be used by vehicles, including roads, footpaths, cycle tracks, loading and servicing areas and vehicle parking space have been fully laid out, surfaced and drained such that loose materials and surface water does not discharge or transfer onto the highway. These areas shall not be used for any other purpose thereafter. To ensure the free and safe use of the highway.

conditions.summary: Construction practice statement
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until a statement of construction practice has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the statement of construction practice shall include full details of: a) the construction vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles and associated traffic management measures. b) methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway from the development hereby approved. c) measures to control the emissions of dust and dirt during construction. d) how the statement of construction practice will be made publicly available by the developer.

conditions.summary: Off-site highway works at Evanston Avenue
conditions.text: Prior to occupation of the development, the off-site highway works as shown in principle on plan 2338-07B comprising an access point with dropped kerb, reinstatement of any redundant dropped kerbs to full height footway and provision of 1.8m wide footway along the entire site frontage at Evanston Avenue shall be fully delivered. To ensure the free and safe use of the highway.

conditions.summary: Electric Vehicle Charging Points provision
conditions.text: The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until the approved Electric Vehicle Charging Points, cable enabled spaces and associated infrastructure have been provided. The facilities shall thereafter be retained and maintained as approved for the lifetime of the development. In the interest of promoting low carbon transport.

conditions.summary: Bin stores and waste storage provision
conditions.text: The approved details for the provision of bin stores (including siting, materials and means of enclosure) and (where applicable) storage of wastes and access for their collection shall be implemented in full before the use commences and shall be retained thereafter as such for the lifetime of the development. In the interests of amenity and to ensure adequate measures for the storage and collection of wastes are put in place.

conditions.summary: Landscaping in accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with details on plans ref: 2338/07A Proposed Site Plan, PWP-766-001 03 Outline Landscape Masterplan and maintained in accordance with the approved details for the lifetime of the development. To ensure the provision and establishment of acceptable landscaping.

conditions.summary: Landscape management plan
conditions.text: A landscape management plan, including long term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the occupation of the development. The Management Plan must conform to Leeds City Council's Landscape Management Plans (Landscape Guidance No.2) and associated checklist. The landscape management plan shall be for the lifetime of the development and shall be carried out as approved. To ensure successful aftercare of landscaping.

conditions.summary: Biodiversity assessment and ecological management plans
conditions.text: No development shall take place until bio-diversity assessment and ecological management plans, including long-term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules for all landscaped areas has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority. These plans shall be carried out as approved and any subsequent variations shall be agreed in writing by the local planning authority. The schemes shall include the following elements: (a) a lighting strategy for minimising light spill onto the river during construction works (b) a lighting strategy for the permanent development, to include location of any proposed lighting, details of any physical modifications to prevent light spill (eg. cowls), details of the intensity and colour range of the lighting and details of any timers and or other control systems. (c) details of new habitat created on-site, as proposed in the ecological impact assessment (d) details of habitat management of the riverbank (e) details of management responsibilities. To ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat. Also, to secure opportunities for enhancing the site's nature conservation value in line with national planning policy and adopted policy G9 of the Leeds Core Strategy (as amended 2019).

conditions.summary: Removal of tarpaulin from riverbank
conditions.text: Prior to development of the site, the plastic tarpaulin, as identified in the Ecological Assessment, on the river bank, shall be removed from site. To ensure the protection of wildlife and supporting habitat. Also, to secure opportunities for enhancing the site's nature conservation value in line with national planning policy and adopted policy G9 of the Leeds Core Strategy (as amended 2019).

conditions.summary: Phase II Site Investigation and Remediation Strategy
conditions.text: The approved Phase I Desk Study report indicates that a Phase II Site Investigation is necessary, and therefore development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Phase II Site Investigation Report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where remediation measures are shown to be necessary in the Phase II Report and/or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Remediation Strategy demonstrating how the site will be made suitable for the intended use has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all works and for the provision of Verification Reports.

conditions.summary: Management of unexpected contamination
conditions.text: If remediation is unable to proceed in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy, or where significant unexpected contamination is encountered, or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, the Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately and operations on the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. An amended or new Remediation Strategy and/or Soil Importation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any further remediation works which shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the revised approved Strategy.

conditions.summary: Remediation works and verification reports
conditions.text: Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. It is strongly recommended that all reports are prepared and approved by a suitably qualified and competent person. To ensure that the remediation works are fully implemented as agreed and the site has been demonstrated to be 'suitable for use' with respect to land contamination.

conditions.summary: Coal mining risk intrusive investigations and remediation
conditions.text: No above ground development shall commence until; a) a scheme of intrusive investigations has been carried out on site to establish the risks posed to the development by past shallow coal mining activity; and b) any remediation works and/or mitigation measures to address land instability arising from past coal mining legacy, as may be necessary, have been implemented on site in full in order to ensure that the site is made safe and stable for the development proposed. The intrusive site investigations, remedial works and mitigatory measures shall be carried out in accordance with authoritative UK guidance.

conditions.summary: Coal mining remediation completion certificate
conditions.text: Prior to the occupation of the development, or it being taken into beneficial use, a signed statement or declaration prepared by a suitably competent person confirming that the site is, or has been made, safe and stable for the approved development shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. This document shall confirm the methods and findings of the intrusive site investigations and the completion of any remedial works and/or mitigation necessary to address the risks posed by past coal mining activity.

conditions.summary: Ground gas monitoring and revised risk assessment
conditions.text: The Coal Mining Risk Assessment report indicates that an Intrusive Site Investigation is necessary including ground gas monitoring. Therefore, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a report presenting the findings of the ground gas monitoring and a revised Ground Gas Risk Assessment (GGRA) has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. Where remediation measures are shown to be necessary in the revised GGRA, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Remediation Strategy demonstrating how the site will be made suitable for the intended use has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all works and for the provision of Verification Reports.

conditions.summary: Contingency for unexpected contamination
conditions.text: If remediation is unable to proceed in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy, or where significant unexpected contamination is encountered, or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, the Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately and operations on the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. An amended or new Remediation Strategy and/or Soil Importation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any further remediation works which shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the revised approved Strategy.

conditions.summary: Remediation verification and site completion
conditions.text: Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures and arboricultural method statement
conditions.text: a) No works shall commence until all existing trees, hedges, bushes shown to be retained on the approved plans are fully safeguarded by protective fencing and ground protection in accordance with approved plans (as approved pursuant to b) below) and specifications and the provisions of British Standard 5837 (2012) Trees in relation to design, demolition and construction, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. NOTE: Only the BS5837 default barrier with the scaffold framework shall be employed. A fully dimensioned tree protection plan drawing shall be included in the submission. Such measures shall be retained for the duration of any demolition and/or approved works. b) No works or development shall commence until a written Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS), including an annotated plan drawing showing all tree protection measures, in accordance with BS5837 for a tree care plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

conditions.summary: Integral bat roosting and bird nesting features
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of development, a Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority of: integral bat roosting and integral bird nesting features (for species such as House Sparrow and Swift) within buildings. Features that are not integral will only be considered for approval if an appropriately qualified ecologist provides assurance that, following discussions with the building architect, integral features are not possible. The agreed Plan shall show the number, specification of the bird nesting and bat roosting features and where they will be located, together with a timetable for implementation and commitment to being installed under the instruction of an appropriately qualified bat consultant. All approved features shall be installed prior to first occupation of the dwelling on which they are located and retained in the manner as approved thereafter.

conditions.summary: Landscape and Biodiversity Net Gain Management Plan
conditions.text: Prior to the commencement of development, a Landscape and Biodiversity Net Gain Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The Plan shall deliver a minimum of 0.19 Habitat Units; on land identified in the Headline Results for On-site Post-Intervention in the Biodiversity Accounting Assessment Report that illustrates the post development Biodiversity Units and include details of the following: a) Description of features to be managed to include Baseline Metric calculations of Biodiversity Units with Condition assessments and UKHab mapping b) Extent and location/area of proposed features and Biodiversity Units on scaled maps and plans using UKHab mapping, with Target Condition assessments and Metric calculations c) Ecological trends and constraints on site that might influence management d) Aims and Objectives of management to include Target Biodiversity Units and Target Condition Criteria e) Appropriate management Actions for achieving Aims and Objectives f) A dated Annual Work Programme (to cover the initial 5 year period) g) Details of the specialist ecological management body/organisation responsible for implementation of the Plan h) How the Plan is to be funded and confirmation from the landowner that it can be delivered i) For each of the first 5 years of the Plan, a progress report sent to the LPA, within 3 months of each year being completed, by an appropriately qualified ecological consultant j) Confirmation that habitat monitoring will be carried out in years 1, 3, 5,10, 20 and 30 and how this will be funded k) The Plan shall set out how contingencies and/or remedial action will be identified, agreed and implemented when necessary l) The Plan will be reviewed and updated every 5 years and implemented for the lifetime of the development m) The approved Plan will be implemented in full accordance with the approved details.

conditions.summary: Drainage works implementation

conditions.summary: Commencement within three years
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

conditions.summary: Accordance with approved plans
conditions.text: The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans listed in the Plans and Specifications above.

conditions.summary: Highway condition survey and remedial works
conditions.text: The development shall not commence until a condition survey of Main Street and South Approach has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. A plan showing the surveyed areas shall also accompany the survey report. Periodic surveys shall also be undertaken every 3 months and then upon completion of the development (completion of the final approved building on the site) a further condition survey shall be carried out and submitted to the Local Planning Authority together with a schedule of remedial works to rectify damage to the highway identified between the two surveys as a result of the development. The approved mitigation works shall be fully implemented within 3 months of the remedial works being agreed with the Local Planning Authority. If a defect is identified during other routine inspections of the highway that is considered to be a danger to the public, then it must immediately be made safe and repaired within 24 hours from the applicant being notified by the Local planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Construction Traffic Management Plan
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until a Construction Traffic Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Construction Traffic Management Plan shall include full details of: (a) The construction vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles. (b) Proposed traffic management measures on the routes (including South Approach) to site for construction traffic including temporary speed limits, suitable temporary signage and road markings. (c) Banned vehicle routing (i.e. left turn out of South Approach/Main Street junction towards Aberford and banned movements during special events (i.e. Leeds Festival)). (d) Proposed measures to mitigate the impact of HGVs on the local road network including measures to minimise and manage HGV movements. (e) Methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway from the development hereby approved. (f) Measures to control the emissions of dust and dirt during construction. (g) How the statement of construction practice will be made publicly available by the developer. (h) A delivery management plan during the construction phase.

conditions.summary: Decommissioning Management Plan
conditions.text: Decommissioning shall not commence until a Decommissioning Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Decommissioning Management Plan shall include full details of: (a) The vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles and associated traffic management measures. (b) Methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway from the development hereby approved. (c) Measures to control the emissions of dust and dirt during decommissioning. (d) How the Decommissioning Management Plan will be made publicly available by the developer. (e) A delivery management plan during the decommissioning phase.

conditions.summary: Access sightlines and visibility splays
conditions.text: The access hereby approved shall not be brought into use until works have been undertaken to provide the sightlines / visibility splays shown on the approved plan ref SYS_VS_001 (included as Appendix B of the Response to Highways Consultation Comments); to an adoptable standard. These sightlines / visibility splays shall be retained clear of all obstruction to visibility greater than 0.6m in height above the adjoining carriageway for the lifetime of the development.

conditions.summary: Construction working hours
conditions.text: Construction works, including deliveries, shall take place only between: 07:00 to 19:00 Monday to Friday; 08:00 to 16:00 Saturday; with no works on Sundays or Bank Holidays.

conditions.summary: Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan
conditions.text: The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan (ref: AWA7449AMS) prepared by AWA Tree Consultants.

conditions.summary: Tree protection measures installation
conditions.text: No works shall commence until the measures to protect existing vegetation as set out in the approved Arboricultural Method Statement (ref: AWA7449AMS - prepared by AWA Tree Consultants) are in place, including the installation of all protection fencing and ground protection measures as specified by the AMS. The protection measures shall be retained for the entirety of the construction phase with exclusion zones enforced to ensure no equipment, machinery or materials shall be used, stored or burnt within any protected area nor shall any ground levels within these zones be altered, nor any excavations undertaken including the provision of any underground services.

conditions.summary: Arboricultural supervision for Root Protection Areas
conditions.text: All works within Root Protection Areas shall be undertaken under the supervision of a suitably qualified arboricultural consultant. A schedule of supervision visits and associated reports shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination discovery protocol
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately where unexpected significant contamination is encountered during any development works and operations in the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. Where remediation of unexpected significant contamination is considered by the Local Planning Authority to be necessary, a Remediation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the recommencement of development on the affected part of the site. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all remediation works and for the provision of verification information. Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all necessary verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. In the event that no unexpected significant contamination is encountered, written confirmation shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority prior to occupation of the site.

conditions.summary: Testing of imported soil and fill materials
conditions.text: Any soil or soil forming materials brought to site for use in garden areas, soft landscaping, public open space or for filling and level raising shall be tested for contamination and suitability for use. A methodology for testing these soils shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to these materials being imported onto site. The methodology shall include information on the source of the materials, sampling frequency, testing schedules and criteria against which the analytical results will be assessed (as determined by risk assessment). Testing shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved methodology.

conditions.summary: National Gas Asset Protection Plan
conditions.text: No development shall commence until a National Gas Asset Protection Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, in consultation with National Gas Transmission. The National Gas Asset Protection Plan shall include an Earthing Study, Lightning Strike Risk Assessment and reenergisation survey. The construction and operation of the site shall be carried out only in accordance with the approved National Gas Asset Protection Plan.

conditions.summary: Post energisation survey for pipeline cathodic protection
conditions.text: Within 3 months of being brought into use, a post energisation survey to assess the effects of the energisation on the pipeline's cathodic protection system should be carried out and the results submitted in a report to the local planning authority to be approved in consultation with NGT. In the interests of visual amenity.

conditions.summary: Statement of Construction Practice
conditions.text: Development shall not commence until a Statement of Construction Practice has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Statement of Construction Practice shall include full details of: a) Demolition/construction vehicle routing, means of access, location of site compound, storage and parking (including workforce parking), means of loading and unloading of all contractors' plant, equipment, materials and vehicles and associated traffic management measures; b) Largest vehicle attending site during demolition/construction c) Methods to prevent mud, grit and dirt being carried on to the public highway from the development hereby approved. d) Measures to control the emissions of dust and dirt during demolition/construction. e) How the Statement of Construction Practice will be made publicly available by the developer. f) Hours of demolition/construction should be clearly defined. The approved details shall be implemented at the commencement of works on site and shall thereafter be retained and employed until completion of the works on site. The Statement on Construction Practice shall be made publicly available for the lifetime of the demolition/construction phase of the development in accordance with the approved method of publicity.

conditions.summary: Phase II Site Investigation and Remediation Strategy
conditions.text:
The approved Phase I Desk Study report indicates that a Phase II Site Investigation is necessary, and therefore development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Phase II Site Investigation Report has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Where remediation measures are shown to be necessary in the Phase II Report and/or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, development (excluding demolition) shall not commence until a Remediation Strategy demonstrating how the site will be made suitable for the intended use has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all works and for the provision of Verification Reports.
It is strongly recommended that all reports are prepared and approved by a suitably qualified and competent person.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination notification procedure
conditions.text: If remediation is unable to proceed in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy, or where significant unexpected contamination is encountered, or where soil or soil forming material is being imported to site, the Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately and operations on the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. An amended or new Remediation Strategy and/or Soil Importation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any further remediation works which shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the revised approved Strategy. Prior to the site being brought into use, where significant unexpected contamination is not encountered, the Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing of such.

conditions.summary: Remediation verification and site commencement
conditions.text:
Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
It is strongly recommended that all reports are prepared and approved by a suitably qualified and competent person.

conditions.summary: Unexpected contamination during works
conditions.text: The Local Planning Authority shall be notified in writing immediately where unexpected significant contamination is encountered during any development works and operations in the affected part of the site shall cease. The affected part of the site shall be agreed with the Local Planning Authority in writing. Where remediation of unexpected significant contamination is considered by the Local Planning Authority to be necessary, a Remediation Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the recommencement of development on the affected part of the site. The Remediation Strategy shall include a programme for all remediation works and for the provision of verification information. Remediation works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy. On completion of those works, the Verification Report(s) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the approved programme. The site or phase of a site shall not be brought into use until such time as all necessary verification information has been approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. In the event that no unexpected significant contamination is encountered, written confirmation shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority.

conditions.summary: Testing of imported soil and soil forming materials

A methodology for testing these soils shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to these materials being imported onto site. The methodology shall include information on the source of the materials, sampling frequency, testing schedules and criteria against which the analytical results will be assessed (as determined by risk assessment). Testing shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved methodology. Relevant evidence, assessment and verification information shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority prior to the site or phase of the site being brought into use.

Hard landscape works shall include: (a) proposed finished levels and/or contours, (b) boundary details, gates, means of enclosure and retaining structures, (c) car parking layouts, (d) other vehicle and pedestrian access and circulation areas, (e) hard surfacing areas, (f) minor artefacts and structures (e.g. furniture, play equipment, refuse or other storage units, signs, lighting etc.), (g) existing trees with Root Protection Areas (RPAs) and all other retained vegetation. Soft landscape works shall include: (h) planting plans... (k) drainage proposals, (l) means of and confirmation of delivery of biodiversity net gain on-site. All hard and soft landscaping works shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details, approved implementation programme, British Standard BS 4428:1989 and Leeds City Council website landscape guidance.

conditions.summary: No works to hedgerows/trees/nesting structures March-August
